criterion_scores.reasoning: I checked the main ignore paths and found a load-bearing runtime defect in the pipeline-side guard: `build()` references `ignored` out of scope at line 34, so the privacy/control path cannot complete as written. The hub-side check-ignore handling and fail-closed behavior otherwise look mostly sound, but this defect is major enough to drag correctness well below pass-mid.

All required layers named by the spec are present: pipeline filter, hub generator filter, and pnpm check verifier with a no-checkout skip note. I did not find a missing required section or stub; the issue I found is a correctness/scope bug rather than an omitted capability.

The artifact follows the expected placement and wiring for the scripts shown, uses explicit failure messaging, and does not violate any visible house convention. I did not see a naming/frontmatter/tooling convention break; no house-context ambiguity needed to be resolved here.

This is appropriately defense-in-depth rather than ceremony-heavy: both the generator and verifier guard the same leak path, and there is no obvious duplicated state resurrection or tombstoned decision. The design is lean for the threat being addressed.

The generator and verifier both emit clear privacy-related messages, and the verifier distinguishes skip vs fail-closed paths. I did note that the build_graph scope bug would surface as an opaque runtime failure, so the artifact is not perfectly diagnostic, but it is still generally legible.

defects.description: This reads `ignored` outside the scope where it is defined (`walk_artifacts()` computes it locally). As shown, `build()` will raise NameError when this branch is reached, so the privacy rule that ignored targets count as absent cannot execute reliably and the dirty-checkout vs clean-clone guarantee is broken.

Checked the verifier script’s pnpm check hook: whether it scans all relevant path-bearing fields (nodes.id, edges.src, edges.dst), whether it skips only when no pipeline checkout exists, and whether it actually fails on a hit.
